claims.text: The baseline alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 previously displayed limited amorphous retention.
The baseline alloy exhibited eutectic, primary, and non-eutectic crystallization arrests during cooling and reheating, especially under slower cooling.
The proposed composition is Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15.
Relative to the baseline, the intervention increases Fe from 16 to 22 at.%, increases Co from 16 to 19 at.%, decreases Mn from 16 to 12 at.%, and decreases P from 20 to 15 at.%.
Increasing Fe and Co while reducing Mn and P will decrease the propensity for primary solid-solution crystallization.
Increasing Fe and Co while reducing Mn and P will decrease the propensity for high-temperature phosphide formation.
The composition change will shift solidification toward cooperative, eutectic-dominated growth.
Rapid quenching will suppress elemental segregation and phosphide nucleation in the modified alloy.
Eutectic-dominated growth under rapid quenching will enhance amorphous retention.
The modified alloy will produce a simpler and more thermally stable devitrification sequence during reheating.
Melt spinning at 40 m/s will produce approximately 20 μm ribbons of the modified alloy.
The approximately 20 μm melt-spun modified-alloy ribbons will be fully amorphous.
Upon reheating, the melt-spun modified alloy will exhibit a dominant eutectic transformation.
The modified alloy will have a broader crystallization interval than Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Slower-cooled modified-alloy ingots will segregate into an Fe–Ni–Mn-rich solid solution and P/Cr-rich phosphides.
The eutectic-dominated solidification structure will comprise fine, predominantly rod-like eutectic colonies.
Arc-melted ingots cool at an average rate of 95.9 K/s and a peak rate of up to 215.2 K/s.
The predicted improvement is limited to rapid-quenching conditions such as melt spinning at 40 m/s and approximately 20 μm ribbon thickness.
Under slower ingot cooling or reheating rates other than 20 K/min, the modified alloy may exhibit multiphase crystallization and reduced amorphous stability.
